document.text:
8 FAM 403.1-4 Material Discrepancies (Major name changes)

(CT:CITZ-141; 03-10-2026)

a. A material discrepancy is any name change that is not defined as immaterial in 8 FAM 403.1-5. The applicant must explain any material discrepancies between the name on the application and the name recorded in the evidence of U.S. citizenship/non-citizen U.S. nationality and the evidence of identity (see 22 CFR 51.25).

b. Material discrepancies between the name recorded on the application, the applicant's evidence of U.S. citizenship/non-citizen U.S. nationality, or the evidence of identity must be documented by submission of one or more of the documents listed in this section (see an exception for married names in 8 FAM 403.1-4(C)). Acceptable means of documenting a material name change include (per 22 CFR 51.25):

(1) Court orders or decrees:

(a) Name change orders; or

(b) Divorce decrees;

(2) Certificates of naturalization;

(3) Marriage certificates;

(4) Documentation demonstrating change of name by operation of state law; or

(5) Documentation of customary usage.

NOTE: Evidence of material name changes must be reviewed for evidence of counterfeiting or alteration (see 8 FAM 201.1)

c. The applicant may not continue to use a previous name after a material name change unless the name change documentation specifically permits the applicant to continue using that name (see 8 FAM 403.1-6 regarding “known as” names).

d. The applicant's name is an integral part of her/his identity. Consequently, under 22 CFR 51.23(c), evidence of identity might be required in accordance with Department guidance to establish the name that best identifies the applicant:

(1) If the applicant has had a material name change more than one year prior to applying on form DS-11 but has not updated her/his ID to reflect the material name change, you must suspend the application to request an acceptable ID in the new name. If there is insufficient time to request that the applicant submit acceptable ID prior to urgent or emergency travel, a limited-validity passport may be issued in the requested name;

(2) The applicant generally will need the name change documentation to change the name on her/his ID. You must fully notate the name change documentation prior to returning the documentation, including that the documentation was "seen and returned," to the applicant with the information request letter (IRL); and

(3) Applicants who have had a material name change within one year of applying on a form DS-11 do not need to submit ID in the new name. However, if the ID has not yet been changed, they must submit their name change documentation.

concepts.label: Documentation of Material Discrepancies
concepts.definition: Acceptable documentation required to substantiate a material name change discrepancy.
concepts.quote: Material discrepancies between the name recorded on the application, the applicant's evidence of U.S. citizenship/non-citizen U.S. nationality, or the evidence of identity must be documented by submission of one or more of the documents listed in this section

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies to material discrepancies between the name recorded on the application, the applicant's evidence of U.S. citizenship/non-citizen U.S. nationality, or the evidence of identity, except for married names as provided in 8 FAM 403.1-4(C).
unit_attributes.choice_text: Must be documented by submission of one or more of the following: court orders or decrees (name change orders or divorce decrees); certificates of naturalization; marriage certificates; documentation demonstrating change of name by operation of state law; or documentation of customary usage.
unit_attributes.logic_text: submission of one or more of the documents listed in this section: (1) Court orders or decrees: (a) Name change orders; or (b) Divorce decrees; (2) Certificates of naturalization; (3) Marriage certificates; (4) Documentation demonstrating change of name by operation of state law; or (5) Documentation of customary usage
unit_attributes.object_quote: Material discrepancies between the name recorded on the application, the applicant's evidence of U.S. citizenship/non-citizen U.S. nationality, or the evidence of identity
unit_attributes.object: material discrepancies between name on application, citizenship/nationality evidence, or identity evidence

qualifications.statement: An exception applies for married names in 8 FAM 403.1-4(C).

unit_attributes.statement: Material discrepancies between the name recorded on the application, the applicant's evidence of U.S. citizenship/non-citizen U.S. nationality, or the evidence of identity must be documented by submission of one or more acceptable documents (including court orders or decrees such as name change orders or divorce decrees, certificates of naturalization, marriage certificates, documentation demonstrating change of name by operation of state law, or documentation of customary usage per 22 CFR 51.25), subject to an exception for married names in 8 FAM 403.1-4(C).

oa:hasSelector.oa:exact: a. A material discrepancy is any name change that is not defined as immaterial in 8 FAM 403.1-5. The applicant must explain any material discrepancies between the name on the application and the name recorded in the evidence of U.S. citizenship/non-citizen U.S. nationality and the evidence of identity (see 22 CFR 51.25).

If the applicant has had a material name change more than one year prior to applying on form DS-11 but has not updated her/his ID to reflect the material name change, you must suspend the application to request an acceptable ID in the new name.
must
Applies if the applicant has had a material name change more than one year prior to applying on form DS-11 but has not updated her/his ID to reflect the material name change.

If there is insufficient time to request that the applicant submit acceptable ID prior to urgent or emergency travel, a limited-validity passport may be issued in the requested name
may
